canonical_name: 23 NYCRR Part 500 — Cybersecurity Requirements for Financial Services Companies
description: NYDFS's flagship cybersecurity regulation. Original effective date 1 March 2017 — the first US prudential-style cybersecurity rule for financial-services firms. Imposes a written cybersecurity program + policy + CISO + risk assessment + MFA + incident response + 72-hour notice + annual certification. Substantially expanded by the Second Amendment in 2023.

Major overhaul of Part 500: introduces 'Class A Companies' (largest entities — $20m+ NY revenue + 2,000+ employees globally or $1bn+ global revenue) with enhanced obligations; mandates universal MFA; requires asset-management + data-inventory policy; mandates EDR + centralised logging for Class A; tightens incident response + adds 24-hour ransomware notice + dual sign-off on annual certification; phased implementation with final controls effective 1 Nov 2025.

canonical_name: 23 NYCRR Part 504 — Transaction Monitoring and Filtering Programs
description: NY's prescriptive AML/sanctions transaction-monitoring + sanctions-screening rule for regulated institutions. Effective 1 Jan 2017. Requires risk-based transaction monitoring + watchlist filtering programs; annual certification by Senior Officer of compliance (similar structure to Part 500 §500.17).

canonical_name: 23 NYCRR Part 200 — Virtual Currency Business Activity (BitLicense)
description: NY's bespoke licensing regime for virtual-currency businesses. Effective 2015. Requires NYDFS license to engage in virtual-currency business activity with NY residents. Covers receiving, transmitting, storing, holding, exchanging, issuing, or controlling virtual currency on behalf of another. Coexists with the federal MSB regime + (where applicable) the federal MiCA-equivalent fragmented framework.

canonical_name: NY SHIELD Act 2019 (NY Gen Bus Law §899-bb)
description: Stop Hacks and Improve Electronic Data Security Act. Broadens the definition of 'private information' to include biometric data + access credentials + medical information. Imposes 'reasonable security' requirements on any person / business owning or licensing private info of a NY resident — administrative, technical + physical safeguards. Applies beyond financial services (any business with NY consumer data).

Foundational state statute governing NY-chartered banks + credit unions + money transmitters + check-cashers + mortgage brokers. Grants NYDFS its prudential + conduct authority over the banking sector. Part 500 covers entities operating under the Banking Law.
Governs NY-licensed insurers + reinsurers + producers + adjusters. NYDFS is the prudential + conduct regulator. Part 500 covers entities operating under the Insurance Law.

Consolidated 2011 statute creating NYDFS through merger of the Banking + Insurance Departments. Sets NYDFS's umbrella regulatory + enforcement authority. Part 500 covers entities operating under the Financial Services Law.

NY's broad securities-fraud + investment-protection statute. Empowers the NY Attorney General to investigate + prosecute securities fraud. No requirement to prove intent; civil + criminal sanctions. Frequently used in high-profile NY-AG cyber + crypto enforcement.

Federal statute (15 USC §§6801-6809). Privacy Rule + Safeguards Rule for financial institutions. FTC + federal banking regulators enforce; Part 500 covers similar ground at state level for NY-regulated entities, generally being more prescriptive than the Safeguards Rule.

Federal Reserve Supervision + Regulation letters (notably SR 11-7 model risk management, SR 23-4 third-party risk management, SR 24-2 operational resilience). NY state-chartered banks subject to dual federal + state supervision; Part 500 obligations operate alongside FRB expectations.

canonical_name: New York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS)
description: Integrated prudential + conduct regulator for ~1,500 NY-chartered banks, insurers, money transmitters, mortgage originators, BitLicense holders. The most influential US state-level financial regulator on cyber + virtual-currency. Issued the first US prudential-cyber rule (Part 500) in 2017. With CFPB on pause in 2025 + the SEC pulling back, NYDFS has become a primary US-level enforcer by default.

Enforces the SHIELD Act + Martin Act + general consumer-protection statutes. Active enforcer on data-breach + crypto fraud + AI bias matters. Coexists with NYDFS on supervised entities — NY-AG handles broader consumer + criminal angles.

Dedicated NYDFS division (announced 2023) for examining cybersecurity programs + receiving 72-hour event notices + 24-hour ransomware notices + annual certifications under §500.17. Leads enforcement actions for Part 500 violations.

canonical_name: US Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) — interplay
description: US Treasury sanctions authority. NYDFS Part 504 requires sanctions-screening programs aligned with OFAC SDN + non-SDN lists. Part 500 ransomware-notice obligations interact with OFAC ransomware-payment advisories (Oct 2020 + Sep 2021 updates).
Federal banking regulator. NY state-chartered banks dual-regulated by NYDFS + FRB. Part 500 + FRB SR letters operate side-by-side; FRB on-site exams often consider Part 500 compliance evidence.

canonical_name: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) — interplay
description: Federal banking regulator for nationally-chartered banks. Some NY-chartered banks have national charters; OCC + NYDFS coordinate on cyber + AML supervision in those cases.

canonical_name: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) — Reg S-P + Reg S-ID interplay
description: Federal securities regulator. Reg S-P (privacy) + Reg S-ID (identity theft) + 2023 cyber-disclosure rules for public companies overlap with Part 500 for NY-licensed broker-dealers + investment advisers. Less active 2025 (post-Iowa v. SEC climate-rule abandonment) but cyber rules remain in force.

Recipient of voluntary cyber-incident reports. OFAC + NYDFS encourage Covered Entities to report ransomware + business-email-compromise + nation-state intrusions to IC3 in parallel with NYDFS § 500.17 filings.

DHS agency. Publishes Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) + cyber-threat alerts. Part 500 risk assessments + vulnerability management programs typically reference CISA KEV in remediation prioritisation.

Any person operating under or required to operate under a license, registration, charter, certificate, permit, accreditation, or similar authorisation under the NY Banking Law, Insurance Law, or Financial Services Law. ~1,500 NYDFS-regulated entities. Limited exemptions under §500.19 for very small entities + reinsurers + captive insurers.

Covered Entity with at least $20 million in gross annual revenue in the last 2 fiscal years from NY-business operations AND either (a) over 2,000 employees averaged over the last 2 fiscal years (employees + independent contractors of the entity + its affiliates), or (b) over $1 billion in gross annual revenue averaged over the last 2 fiscal years from all business operations (entity + affiliates). Enhanced obligations apply.

Maintain a written cybersecurity program based on the Risk Assessment. Designed to perform the core functions of identifying + assessing cyber risks; protecting the entity's Information Systems + Nonpublic Information; detecting cybersecurity events; responding + recovering; fulfilling regulatory reporting. Documented + provided to NYDFS on request.

Written cybersecurity policy(ies) approved by the Senior Governing Body (board or equivalent) or, if none, the Senior Officer responsible for the cybersecurity program. Reviewed at least annually + on material change. Must address 14 enumerated topics including information security, data governance, access controls, vendor management, incident response, BCDR.

Designate a qualified CISO with the authority + resources to implement + enforce the cybersecurity program. May be employed by the Covered Entity, an affiliate, or a third-party service provider (with retained responsibility). CISO presents written report at least annually to the Senior Governing Body on the cybersecurity program + material cyber risks + significant cybersecurity events + plans for remediation. NEW under Second Amendment: CISO must have adequate authority to ensure compliance + report timely to Senior Governing Body or Senior Officer on material cyber issues.

Board of directors, equivalent governing body, or where neither exists, the Senior Officer responsible for the cybersecurity program. Under the Second Amendment the Senior Governing Body has explicit oversight responsibilities — sufficient understanding + ensuring management implements program + receiving CISO reports + dual sign-off on annual certification.

Penetration testing of Information Systems at least annually by a qualified internal or external party (with sufficient independence to ensure objective assessment). Automated scans of Information Systems + manual review designed to identify publicly known + identified vulnerabilities. Documented + prioritised remediation based on risk. NEW for Class A: automated scans on a continuous basis.

Securely maintain audit trails designed to detect + respond to cybersecurity events that have a reasonable likelihood of materially harming any material part of normal operations. Retain records: 5 years for material cybersecurity events; 3 years for the audit trail itself.

Limit user access privileges to Information Systems that provide access to Nonpublic Information; periodically (at least annually) review access privileges + remove / disable accounts no longer necessary. NEW under Second Amendment (effective 1 Nov 2025): privileged accounts limited to those reasonably necessary; protections against unauthorized use; MFA on privileged accounts; restrictions on remote privileged access; expiry of privileged-account sessions; secure password policy.

Written procedures, guidelines + standards designed to ensure the use of secure development practices for in-house developed applications + the assessment + testing of externally developed applications used in connection with the Covered Entity's technology environment. Reviewed + updated as necessary at least annually.

Periodic written Risk Assessment of the Covered Entity's Information Systems, sufficient to inform the design of the cybersecurity program. Updated at least annually + whenever a change in the business or technology causes a material change to cyber risk. Considers: criteria for identifying + classifying threats + impacts; mitigation; how identified risks will be addressed.

metadata.frequency: at least annual + on material change

description: Use qualified cybersecurity personnel of the Covered Entity, an affiliate, or a third-party service provider sufficient to manage the cybersecurity risks + perform / oversee performance of core cybersecurity functions; provide cybersecurity personnel with cybersecurity updates + training; verify that key cybersecurity personnel maintain current knowledge of changing threats + countermeasures.

canonical_name: Third Party Service Provider Security Policy (§500.11)
description: Written policy + procedures for security of Information Systems + Nonpublic Information accessible to, or held by, Third Party Service Providers (TPSPs). Risk-based: TPSP identification + risk assessment; minimum cybersecurity practices; due diligence; periodic assessment based on risk; representations + warranties addressing access controls + encryption + breach notification + commitment to maintain cybersecurity practices.

NEW under Second Amendment (effective 1 May 2025): MFA utilised for any individual accessing any Information System of the Covered Entity (not limited to access from external networks). Exceptions: where the CISO has approved in writing the use of reasonably equivalent or more secure compensating controls (reviewed at least annually). Privileged-account access also requires MFA.

NEW under Second Amendment (effective 1 May 2025): written policies + procedures designed to produce + maintain a complete, accurate + documented asset inventory of Information Systems — track changes; track tracked-data-flow + key information (owner, location, classification, support expiration, recovery time objective); retention of data only as long as necessary for business or legal purposes.

Risk-based monitoring + filtering web traffic + email to block malicious content (NEW Class A — endpoint detection + response (EDR) solution + centralised logging + security monitoring, effective 1 Nov 2025). Cybersecurity awareness training at least annually for all personnel — includes social engineering training + relates to risks identified in the Risk Assessment. NEW: secure-development training where applicable; phishing simulations.

Encryption of Nonpublic Information held or transmitted by the Covered Entity, both in transit over external networks + at rest. Where infeasible, the CISO may approve in writing the use of effective alternative compensating controls (reviewed at least annually). NEW under Second Amendment: removes prior 'in lieu of encryption' generic carve-out — alternative controls must be specifically justified.

Written incident response plan(s) designed to respond to + recover from any cybersecurity event materially affecting confidentiality, integrity, or availability of Information Systems or normal business operations. Addresses: internal response processes; roles + responsibilities + decision-making authority; external + internal communications + information sharing; identification of remediation requirements; documentation + reporting; evaluation + revision following an event. NEW under Second Amendment: separate written BCDR plan; both plans tested at least annually (tabletop + technical).

Notice to NYDFS Superintendent as promptly as possible but in no event later than 72 hours from a determination that a cybersecurity event has occurred at the Covered Entity, its affiliates, or a TPSP affecting it, that either: (1) impacts the Covered Entity + notice is required to be provided to any government body, self-regulatory agency, or supervisory body OR (2) has a reasonable likelihood of materially harming any material part of the normal operations of the Covered Entity OR (3) results in deployment of ransomware within a material part of the Covered Entity's Information Systems.

NEW under Second Amendment: Notice to NYDFS Superintendent within 24 hours of any extortion payment made in connection with a cybersecurity event involving the Covered Entity. Plus written description within 30 days of reasons the payment was necessary, alternatives considered, sanctions diligence (OFAC), all diligence performed to find alternatives.

Annually by 15 April: certification of material compliance OR acknowledgement of non-compliance with specific identification of areas + remediation efforts. NEW under Second Amendment: dual sign-off — Senior Officer of the Covered Entity AND the highest-ranking executive of the Covered Entity (or alternative as approved by Superintendent). Material records supporting the certification retained for 5 years for examination.

Limited exemptions: (a) Covered Entities with fewer than 20 employees + less than $7.5m in revenue + less than $15m in assets — partial exemption (some §500 obligations apply); (b) certain reinsurers; (c) certain captive insurers; (d) employees / agents / representatives of Covered Entities relying on the Covered Entity's program. File Notice of Exemption with NYDFS to claim.

Civil monetary penalties available under the underlying Banking / Insurance / Financial Services Law (per Financial Services Law §408 — up to $1,000 per violation, with each separate cybersecurity event or non-compliance counting as a violation, potentially multiplied across affected records). NYDFS public consent orders + remediation orders also routine.

Class A Companies must conduct a cybersecurity audit of the Covered Entity's cybersecurity program annually, based on the Risk Assessment, by an internal or external auditor sufficiently independent + qualified. Audit findings + remediation plans reported to Senior Governing Body.
Class A Companies must implement a privileged access management (PAM) solution + an automated method of blocking commonly-used compromised passwords. Effective 1 Nov 2025.

Class A Companies must implement endpoint detection + response (EDR) solution to monitor anomalous activity + centralised logging + security monitoring solution to alert + investigate cybersecurity events. Effective 1 Nov 2025.

canonical_name: Part 504 — Transaction Monitoring + Watchlist Filtering Programs
description: Regulated Institutions (broadly: banks + trust companies + private bankers + check cashers + money transmitters licensed under NY Banking Law) must maintain risk-based transaction monitoring + sanctions / watchlist filtering programs reasonably designed to detect potential violations of BSA/AML laws + OFAC requirements. Senior Officer annual certification (Part 504 §504.4) of compliance.

NY's bespoke licensing regime for virtual-currency businesses. License required to engage in 'virtual currency business activity' involving NY or a NY resident: receiving, transmitting, storing, holding, exchanging, buying/selling on customers' behalf, issuing virtual currency. Part 500 fully applies to BitLicense holders.

canonical_name: NY SHIELD — Reasonable Security Requirement (Gen Bus L §899-bb)
description: Any person or business owning or licensing private information of a NY resident must develop, implement, + maintain reasonable safeguards. Three categories: administrative (e.g. designated coordinator, employee training, risk assessment, vendor selection); technical (e.g. risk assessment of networks, intrusion detection, testing); physical (e.g. risk assessment of physical storage, disposal). Small business proportionality carve-out.

Public consent orders document NYDFS Part 500 enforcement patterns: First American Title (2020 — risk assessment failures), Residential Mortgage Services (2021 — incident notice + Cybersecurity Program), Carnival (2022 — MFA + access controls), Verifone (2024 — TPSP risk management), Geico/Travelers (2022 — quote-platform breaches), Eyemed (2022 — phishing + MFA), PayPal (2025 — quote-platform breach + MFA), Coinbase (2023 — BitLicense + Part 500 + Part 200), Robinhood (2022 — VA + cyber). Total penalties exceeded $150m through 2025.
